angle: one scene where this happens, with one subject in it
subject: A pebble has just dropped into a still, shallow stream, and a plume of silt billows up off the bed where it landed and leans away downstream under rings on the water.
controls: settle: rotation; the plume leans downstream, nearly upright at 0.1 s (it drops before the current can carry it) and leaning about 40 degrees at 10 s.
layers: count; one billow per partial, each its own contour folded over the one above, so the plume goes from two lumps to a fine cauliflower.
stir: shape; the plume's height, the high billows rising furthest, capped under the water surface.
grain: shape; the billows scatter off the column into a ragged, uneven plume (seeded per billow).
reference: library/theseus-tower (line drawing, black bodies with grey outlines, one lit subject)
risks: Single weight: everything is 1.5 px, so hierarchy rests on brightness alone (bright plume outline vs mid-grey scene); a departure from three weights by the direction's own language.
The plume outline at rest can read as a shell or a cabbage; whether it reads as silt depends on the motion (billowing up on a note, leaning and sinking).
Stir and grain are both shape on the plume; they change different things (height vs raggedness) but share the outline path.
